authority: Reading aid derived from the key-moment tables in each canonical shot direction.md; not rendered stills, animation keyframes or an execution release.

shots.title: Expected size, discovered shape
shots.layout: Near-axial comparison. All references stay registered at source scale. Tight area is a separately labelled example.
moments: The expected circle
A complete white nominal bit-size circle is visible around the tool.
Introduce the size reference.
This is the expected size, not the measured wall.
The actual outline
The irregular reconstructed wall appears against the same white circle, with a blue bulge outside it.
Add the source-derived wall shape.
The wall is farther out at this location.
Read the enlargement
The white circle and blue enlarged region hold still together. The gap is easy to compare.
Hold the comparison; add no new data.
Nominal and actual size are different.
A different example
A clear cut introduces example B, with its own complete white circle and its own wall outline.
Change examples explicitly.
This is another illustrative case, not a hole deforming.
Locate the tight area
A small red region lies inside example B's white reference. A restrained locator points to it.
Emphasize only the local inward difference.
This part is smaller than nominal.
Inspect the small difference
A labelled magnified detail shows the same red location while the whole profile remains visible.
Open the source-rendered detail view.
Magnification changes the view, not the geometry.

shots.title: The shape continues
shots.layout: Oblique depth view of a separately identified spiral example. The reconstructed wall becomes the hero.
moments: One cross-section
One irregular profile is prominent. The tool still provides orientation inside it.
Establish the first depth section.
We recognise the kind of shape already shown.
Several depths
The camera is farther back. Several registered cross-sections now recede through depth.
Only the camera withdraws.
The shape has length, not just a circumference.
Follow the changing bulge
The enlarged part occupies a different position around each successive section.
Emphasize that source-derived progression.
The irregularity follows a spiral-like path along the wall.
The space left behind
The full depth view fills the frame. ECCO is now small or near the frame edge.
The camera settles on the discovered space.
The wall shape is the result worth seeing.

shots.title: Another property of the echo
shots.layout: Clean information space around the familiar reconstruction. Geometry and acoustic response use separate labelled views.
moments: Recall the first property
A small timing cue is paired with the blue geometry view: “Travel time: hole shape”.
Briefly recall the established relationship.
Timing supplied the shape information.
Introduce the other property
A separate echo-strength cue is labelled “Echo strength: acoustic response”.
Shift attention to the other property of the returned echo.
This is different information from the same measurement process.
Make a clean separation
The blue geometry display recedes. The acoustic-response label remains in clear space.
Clear the geometry emphasis before the warm result appears.
One colour map is not turning into the other.
The warm image
A separate yellow/brown response surface appears on the reconstructed positions, with visible variation.
Reveal the independently derived strength display.
These colours show acoustic response, not rock's optical colour.
Read the variation
A small camera shift reveals the response on another flank while the mapped features stay fixed.
Only the camera changes view.
The response varies around the wall and through depth.

scope: Section 3 only — format pilot; other sections not expanded.
